original_question: For a modular numerical semigroup S(a, b, 1), find formulas for the Frobenius number F(S(a, b, 1)), multiplicity m(S(a, b, 1)), type t(S(a, b, 1)), and embedding dimension e(S(a, b, 1)) in terms of the parameters a and b.
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Proportionally modular semigroups": the open problem stating that, for the modular numerical semigroup S(a,b,1), a formula for the genus g(S(a,b,1)) is known, but formulas for the Frobenius number F(S(a,b,1)), multiplicity m(S(a,b,1)), type t(S(a,b,1)), and embedding dimension e(S(a,b,1)) remain open.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It identifies the correct family, namely modular numerical semigroups of the form S(a,b,1), and it asks for exactly the four invariants that the paper singles out as still lacking formulas: Frobenius number, multiplicity, type, and embedding dimension. It also correctly does not ask for the genus, which the paper explicitly says is already known for S(a,b,1).
missing_details: The paper’s notation S(a,b,1) must be defined explicitly as the set of nonnegative integer solutions of the modular Diophantine inequality ax mod b <= x, i.e. S(a,b,1) = {x in N : ax mod b <= x}, with N = {0,1,2,...}.
The operator "ax mod b" should be specified as the least nonnegative residue of ax modulo b.

The parameter range should be made explicit: a and b are positive integers, and using the normalization discussed in Section 2 one may assume 1 < a < b, since S(a,b,c) = N when a <= c and replacing a by a mod b does not change the solution set.
The ambient object should be stated: S(a,b,1) is a numerical semigroup, i.e. a cofinite submonoid of N under addition.
Multiplicity should be defined, e.g. m(S) is the least positive element of S (equivalently the first element of the unique minimal system of generators).
Embedding dimension should be defined as the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S.
Type should be defined through pseudo-Frobenius numbers: t(S) = |PF(S)|, where PF(S) = {f in Z \ S : f + s in S for all s in S \ {0}}.
To be paper-faithful, the question should note that this is posed as an open problem in the paper, not as a theorem with known formulas.
To sharpen the scope, it helps to say explicitly that the genus g(S(a,b,1)) is excluded because the paper states that a formula for it is already known.
refined_question: Let N = {0,1,2,...}, and for positive integers a and b define the modular numerical semigroup S(a,b,1) := {x in N : ax mod b <= x}, where ax mod b denotes the least nonnegative residue of ax modulo b. Using the standard reduction noted for proportionally modular semigroups, one may assume 1 < a < b. Determine explicit formulas, in terms of a and b, for the Frobenius number F(S(a,b,1)), the multiplicity m(S(a,b,1)), the type t(S(a,b,1)) = |PF(S(a,b,1))|, and the embedding dimension e(S(a,b,1)) of S(a,b,1), where PF(S) = {f in Z \ S : f + s in S for all s in S \ {0}} and e(S) is the size of the unique minimal system of generators of S. (The genus g(S(a,b,1)) is excluded, since the paper notes that a formula for it is already known.)
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. Section 2 defines proportionally modular inequalities ax mod b <= cx and the associated semigroups S(a,b,c), then specializes to the modular case c = 1 and explicitly states that a formula for g(S(a,b,1)) is known while formulas for F(S(a,b,1)), m(S(a,b,1)), t(S(a,b,1)), and e(S(a,b,1)) remain open. Section 2 also records the normalization facts making c < a < b nonrestrictive, which in the modular case become 1 < a < b. Section 1 supplies the meanings of numerical semigroup, Frobenius number, multiplicity, embedding dimension, pseudo-Frobenius numbers, and type. Unlike the generic template mentioned in the instructions, this paper has no Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the exact target is this open-problem paragraph in Section 2.
